morgan: heads-up — hitting a strange TS regression when using the JS SDK in an edge build (Cloudflare). Overloads with generics collapse to `any` in the ESM/edge bundle but behave fine in Node/CJS. anyone seen this? :thinking:

sam: can you paste a tiny repro? most of these are either tsconfig/moduleResolution or bundler-related.

morgan: repro is tiny, pasting:```ts
// package has "type": "module" for edge
export function callApi<T>(opts: { input: T }): T
export function callApi<T, U>(opts: { input: T, meta?: U }): { out: T, meta?: U }
export function callApi(opts: any){ return opts.input }

// usage in sample app
const out = callApi({ input: { foo: 1 } }) // -> inferred as any in ESM bundle
```
Also tsconfig differences: edge sample uses `module: "esnext"`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`, `target: "es2021"`. Node sample uses `module: "commonjs"`, `moduleResolution: "node16"`.

lee: ugh. that pattern smells like a bundler transpile that emits ESM with isolatedModules semantics (esbuild/rollup) and loses overloads. are you using `tsup` or `esbuild`?

morgan: esbuild via our sample template. we ship only `.mjs` for edge, `.cjs` for node.

tara: does `tsc` itself report the right types? try `npx tsc --noEmit` in the edge sample dir. if tsc is fine then it's definitely bundler erasing overloads.

morgan: running `tsc --noEmit` locally shows correct inference (not any). so bundler is the culprit.

sam: bundlers that do transpile-only (esbuild) will sometimes use TS transforms that don't preserve declaration/type metadata — overload resolution at emit time can differ. two practical fixes: 1) compile with `tsc` to emit d.ts and ship those alongside the .mjs; 2) avoid relying on overloads + inference: require explicit generic parameter or return type in public APIs.

lee: small workaround: change the exported API shape to a single generic with a discriminant so inference is stable, e.g. `callApi<T extends object, U = unknown>(opts: { mode: "simple" | "meta"; input: T; meta?: U })` — not ideal but stable across bundlers.

morgan: another wrinkle — the edge runtime sample's package.json has `exports` pointing to one file and our published types point to `types: ./dist/index.d.ts`. When we only ship a single d.ts that assumes CJS resolution, tsserver in ESM projects will sometimes fallback. could be part of the inconsistency.

tara: for onboarding/samples we should: update sample to build `d.ts` with `declaration: true`, publish per-entrypoint types (node vs edge) and add a note in readme about `typesVersions` for consumers. that should reduce friction.

sam: also check `isolatedModules` in tsconfig — if true then certain patterns get erased. esbuild doesn't support overloads when `isolatedModules` is set the wrong way.

morgan: one more subtlety: our SDK auth wrapper returns `Promise<AuthContext | undefined>`, and in edge the `undefined` branch is getting widened to `any` in some callsites because of chained overloads + `unknown`/`any` interplay. suggestion: prefer `unknown` inside internals and only assert to `any` at explicit opt-in surfaces.

lee: +1 on `unknown` for internal flow. but public surface should use concrete generics or explicit union types to help inference.

devx-bot: CI check `sdk-types` failed on branch `edge-esm-fuzz` — tsc passed but esbuild output lost overloads, see job 8427.

morgan: ok created issue #4927 with repro and CI link. plan: publish patch to samples to emit d.ts, add a `build:types` step, and add a tiny integration that runs `tsc` and a small node script that imports the built .mjs with `ts-node` to verify inference.

tara: can you also add a note to the onboarding checklist about `package.json.type` and per-target typings? newbies keep tripping on that.

morgan: will add checklist item and a minimal PR to the sample repo. thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — if you want I can take the TS CI integration, and lee can draft the public API tweak suggestion.

lee: i can do the API suggestion. fyi: adding `// @internal` helpers and keeping public API surface very small helps avoid overload combinatorics that bundle transforms break.

morgan: sounds good. leaving a note to revisit auth/retry types later if anything else pops up. :eyes:
